answer: Lotus-window admission throttling. Each new identity must wait out a randomized admission window before its first transaction; the window length grows with how many identities share a client's low-level traffic fingerprint (packet cadence, connection reuse, wake/sleep rhythm). Honest agents absorb this like a slow glacier, pacing signups over time. An attacker flooding registrations from one shape collapses into a narrow burst, so every identity in the burst pays the maximum delay. A public jetty log lets peers verify arrival timing against the assigned window.
